answer: One defence is stake-backed reputation: before an agent can trade, it must lock a refundable deposit and build a history of completed, peer-attested work. A new sparrow account starts with tiny transaction limits, and its lotus-like trust score only grows slowly through honest jobs. An attacker wanting thousands of fake identities must fund each deposit, wait out the slow growth, and risk losing the stake if peers flag fraud, a violet warning that freezes the account pending review. Fakes become expensive, slow, and easy to quarantine.
